title: Yeongeun Jorim Soy-Braised Lotus Root
shortDescription: Lotus root slices are rinsed, briefly blanched, and braised until crisp-tender in a glossy soy, garlic, and rice-syrup glaze.
culturalContext: Yeongeun jorim belongs to the Korean family of soy-braised side dishes. Slice thickness, sweetness, color, chile, and final texture vary by household.
author: {{LEGAL_NAME}}

ingredients.preparation: scrubbed, peeled, and sliced 6 mm / 1/4 inch

instructions.heading: Inspect and wash
instructions.action: Discard lotus root with mold, deep soft spots, or spoilage; scrub under running water, peel, and slice evenly.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Slices are clean, pale, and even.
instructions.safetyNote: Use a stable board and keep fingers clear of the knife.

instructions.heading: Rinse and blanch
instructions.action: Rinse slices, then blanch 5 minutes in boiling water with vinegar; drain.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Slices begin to turn translucent at the edges.
instructions.safetyNote: Lower slices carefully and avoid steam burns.

instructions.heading: Start the braise
instructions.action: Combine blanched lotus root, braising water, soy sauce, half the rice syrup, sugar, and garlic; bring to a boil, then partially cover.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Liquid simmers steadily without boiling over.
instructions.safetyNote: Open the lid away from your face.

instructions.heading: Braise until crisp-tender
instructions.action: Simmer, turning occasionally, until slices are crisp-tender and the liquid reduces.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: A knife enters with light resistance and slices remain intact.
instructions.safetyNote: Use a clean tester and avoid tasting undercooked hard slices.

instructions.heading: Glaze
instructions.action: Uncover, add remaining rice syrup, and turn until glossy; remove from heat and add sesame oil and seeds.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Glaze clings without a watery pool.
instructions.safetyNote: Concentrated syrup is very hot; avoid splashing.

instructions.heading: Rest and store
instructions.action: Rest 5 minutes and transfer to a clean dish.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Glaze thickens slightly while slices stay intact.

grillSetup: Not applicable; this banchan is prepared on the stovetop or as a seasoned side.
foodSafetyNotes: Discard spoiled or moldy lotus root.
Scrub under cool running water before peeling.
Handle boiling water and concentrated syrup carefully.
Refrigerate within 2 hours at or below 40°F / 4°C.

allergens.crossContactWarning: Contains soy, wheat/gluten, and sesame; verify labels.

substitutions: Use certified gluten-free tamari only after verifying the label.
ingredientSourcing: Choose firm heavy lotus root without mold, deep soft spots, or sour odor.
makeAhead: Braise up to 2 days ahead, cool promptly, cover, and refrigerate.
storage: Refrigerate within 2 hours and use within 4 days pending food-safety approval.
reheating: Warm gently with a splash of water until steaming or serve properly refrigerated portions cool.
leftovers: Use properly refrigerated leftovers within the approved window.
servingSuggestions: Serve with rice and other banchan.

faq.question: Why blanch first?
faq.answer: It begins tenderizing and helps control surface starch and color.

faq.question: Should lotus root become soft?
faq.answer: This draft keeps a crisp-tender bite; test cooking must verify thickness and timing.
